s.g: (medicine) Any substance which absorbs and neutralizes acid fluid in the stomach and bowels, as magnesia, chalk, etc.; also a substance, e.g., iodine, which acts on the absorbent vessels so as to reduce enlarged and indurated parts.

A Germanic language descending from Dutch; the primary language of the descendants of Dutch and other European settlers, as well as many mixed-race (e.g. Rehoboth Basters) living in South Africa and in Namibia. Also, one of the eleven official languages of South Africa and until 1990 one of three official languages of Namibia.

A semitransparent, uncrystallized silicate mineral and semiprecious stone, presenting various tints in the same specimen, with colors delicately arranged and often curved in parallel alternating dark and light stripes or bands, or blended in clouds; various authorities call it a variety of chalcedony, a variety of quartz, or a combination of the two.
An aircraft landing field, usually with one runway and only basic facilities.
(organic chemistry) Any of a series of univalent radicals of the general formula CnH2n+1 derived from aliphatic hydrocarbons. In other words, an alkane minus one hydrogen atom.
(pharmaceutical effect) Capable of preventing microbial infection.
Of or relating to ascetics.
Any of several plants of the genus Aster; one of its flowers.
A gradual diminishing of strength.
A member of nomadic Arab tribes dwelling in the desert.
Someone who observes or beholds; an observer or spectator.
A sweet chewing gum formulated to be stretchy so the chewer can blow bubbles with it.
A belch.
To emit a burp.
To thoroughly examine or investigate (something) physically or by discussion; to debate, to gather opinion, to scrutinize.
device for separation of substances
A padded cover for a bed, duvet, continental quilt.
One to whom is committed some charge, duty, or office, by a superior power; a commissioner.

A mixture prepared in such a way.
To secretly plot or make plans together, often with the intention to bring bad or illegal results; to collude, to connive, to plot.
Amazement or horror that confounds the faculties, and incapacitates for reflection; terror, combined with amazement; dismay.
A musical instrument of the brass family, slightly smaller than a trumpet, usually in the musical key of B-flat.
A piece of paper twisted to be used as a container.
A tractor crawler, a motorized vehicle that uses caterpillar tracks instead of wheels.
A process (a running program) that does not have a controlling terminal.
A public hall for dancing.
Unreasonably or stubbornly resisting change.
Complete; having no opposite opinion of anything in a particular topic of one's values; thorough of in one's beliefs.

A dissolute course of life, in which health, money, etc., are squandered in pursuit of pleasure; profuseness in immoral indulgence, as late hours, riotous living, etc.; dissoluteness.
The act of dissipating or dispersing; a state of dispersion or separation; dispersion; waste.

A dummy or other crude representation of a person, group or object that is hated.
The scientific study of insects, and (informal) of other arthropods (and occasionally other invertebrates).
Excessive or superfluous expenditure of money.
(nautical) A carved figure on the prow of a sailing ship.

An open channel or trough used to direct or divert liquids, especially to carry materials (logs, mined material, etc) or people (as a water slide), especially (but not always) one where the walls are raised above the surrounding terrain rather than recessed like a ditch.
(UK, Irish, Commonwealth, Philippines) A road or railway that passes over another, allowing routes to cross without interruption.
A belt or sash at the waist, often used to support stockings or hosiery.
(transitive) To fill to capacity; to satisfy all demand or requirement; to sate.
An excess, too much.
Not acknowledging any deity or god; without belief in any deity or god.
(obsolete, transitive) To pinch; to distress. Specifically, to cause pinching and spasmodic pain to the bowels of, as by the effects of certain purgative or indigestible substances.
A complaint, often a petty or trivial one.
(obsolete) Grasp; clutch; grip.
(obsolete) That which is grasped; a handle; a grip.
(chiefly, in the plural) Pinching and spasmodic pain in the intestines.
A (commercial) facility where eggs, especially those of fish or poultry, are hatched under artificial conditions.
A mound, pile, or stack of stored hay.
In the shape of a helix.
A pipe with a long flexible tube that draws the smoke through water, traditionally used for smoking tobacco, which is often flavored.
(derogatory, now, offensive) A person with a humpback; a person who suffers from kyphosis.
A humped back (deformity in humans caused by abnormal curvature of the upper spine).
The ordinal form of the number one hundred.
Pertaining to or having the nature of fire; containing fire; resembling fire.
Those qualities or features that are imperfect; the characteristic, state, or quality of being imperfect.
Something that makes something else less than perfect; a blemish, impurity, error, etc.

Anas platyrhynchos, a common and widespread dabbling duck, natively found throughout the Northern Hemisphere, whose male has a distinctive dark green head.
An island in the Mediterranean; largest of the Balearic Islands.

An intermediate floor or storey in between the main floors of a building; specifically, one that is directly above the ground floor which does not extend over the whole floorspace of the building, and so resembles a large balcony overlooking the ground floor; an entresol.

Any of numerous hemiparasitic evergreen plants of the order Santalales with white berries that grow in the crowns of apple trees, oaks, and other trees, such as the European mistletoe (Viscum album) and American mistletoe or eastern mistletoe (Phoradendron leucarpum).
